newsitem.title: USA: O.J. Simpson jury asks to see blood evidence.
newsitem.headline: O.J. Simpson jury asks to see blood evidence.

text.p: Jurors in O.J. Simpson's civil trial indicated on Thursday they were closely examining the defence claim that blood was planted by police to frame the ex-football star and evidence was contaminated.

The panel, in its third day of deliberations, asked to see a series of enlarged photographs and six large evidence boards containing more pictures. They also requested three photos of blood stains found on the rear gate to Nicole Brown Simpson's condominium that matched Simpson's blood, which the defence claims were planted by police.

Simpson was acquitted of the June 12, 1994, murders of his ex-wife and her friend, Ronald Goldman, by a criminal court jury in October 1995. In the civil trial, he is battling a wrongful-death lawsuit brought by the families of the victims, who are seeking substantial damages.

The jury also wanted to see a board showing several gruesome pictures of the victims taken hours after their deaths as well as photos of the bloody glove found in a narrow walkway on Simpson's estate and a plan of the grounds.
Simpson's defence team has maintained that the glove was planted by former detective Mark Fuhrman, whom they have described as a rogue cop out to frame the former athlete.

Fuhrman, who is white, was discredited in the criminal case when Simpson's defence proved he lied when he testified he had not used the racial slur "nigger" in the past 10 years. He later pleaded no contest to a single charge of perjury and was fined and placed on probation.

Among the boards requested was one containing photos of the DNA test strips on blood taken from the centre console of Simpson's white Ford Bronco. The tests showed that the blood contained the DNA of both Simpson and Goldman, but an expert called by the defence said the test results were suspect because the sample had been contaminated.

Simpson's lead attorney, Robert Baker, also claimed in his closing argument to the jury last week that police broke into the Bronco and smeared blood taken from the reference blood samples of Simpson and Goldman.

The jury also requested the DNA test strips on the blood samples of Nicole Brown Simpson and Goldman, drawn after their deaths. The defence expert testified that their blood also contained barely detectable traces of Simpson's DNA.

They also requested a photo of the DNA test strip on a single drop of blood at the murder scene that was also a match for Simpson's blood. That was the only blood from the scene tested by the more exhaustive DNA test known as RFLP. It was also the subject of a defence claim that it had been planted.

The jury deliberated for just over eight hours on Tuesday and Wednesday, poring over other evidence pictures with the use of a photographic magnifying glass and examining a test tube similar to the one used to store Simpson's blood sample taken by police the day after Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman were stabbed and slashed to death.

Should the panel find Simpson liable for the murders, they must also assess compensatory damages before announcing their verdict. If the verdict goes against Simpson, a second phase of the trial will follow in which the jury will be asked to decide how much he must pay in additional damages to punish him for his actions.
